utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Can you hear me clearly in your own language?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Witness, please state your name for the Court.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: My name is Ivan Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Grujic's expert report and his testimony from the Milosevic case have already been admitted in this case in the decision of 13th January, 2006. As a result, in my examination, I will question the witness mainly on various exhibits. But by way of a brief introduction I would like to point out that Mr. Grujic is a Croatian citizen who was appointed president of the Republic of Croatia Commission for Detainees and Missing Persons in 1993. He held this post until the year 2000 when the commission was abolished and the Republic of Croatia Government Office for Detainees and Missing Persons was founded. In the year 2000 Mr. Grujic was appointed head of the office. In January 2004 the office was replaced by the Administration for Detainees and Missing Persons located within the Ministry of Family, Defenders and Intergeneration Solidarity.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, could you briefly summarise your education and work experience prior to 1993.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to primary and secondary school in Osijek, and after that I did my military service in the JNA where I was trained to be a military policeman. And after that I found a job with the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia where I worked on jobs requiring secondary schooling, after which I completed a higher school and an intelligence school, which qualified me for jobs requiring higher education, on which I worked until 1992. I did various jobs, beginning with policeman, until inspector first class, on jobs that had to do with anti-terrorism and intelligence. After that, I went to the higher criminological school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: What is your present position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Currently I am assistant minister at the Ministry of Intergenerational Solidarity, and I'm also president of the government Commission for Missing Persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: What is the scope of the work of this government Commission for Missing Persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The Commission for Missing Persons is a technical advisory body of the government dealing with issues of missing persons. And on the level of assistant ministers it involves all relevant ministries that are able to gather data on missing persons; the public prosecutor's office, the MUP, the Ministry of Defence, the Red Cross, and various security agencies. This advisory body charts a strategy to be followed in the search for missing persons, people who went missing during the homeland war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: As head of the Commission for Detainees and Missing Persons, a position to which you were appointed in 1993, and later as head of the Office for Detainees and Missing Persons, what did your work involve?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I'll try to explain briefly. In 1993 the government of the Republic of Croatia set up a commission for the search for missing persons. And from that day on several modes of organisation changed in that commission following changes in the government. But the tasks boiled down to the search for missing persons, and that involves negotiations with representatives of the countries of the former Yugoslavia who are able to have information about missing persons, as well as exhumations of individual and mass graves in areas that used to be occupied, but also the monitoring of exhumations in Serbia and Montenegro and Bosnia and Herzegovina where we are involved as monitors. And apart from that, one of the tasks of our administration is to conduct identification of exhumed bodies, and of course to keep all possible records about missing persons, about exhumations, records of identified remains from mass graves, official records on prisoners of war who had been released from camps and prisons. And that is also one of the tasks of this administration which used to be a commission earlier. And also when keeping records of missing persons, we obtain data also about displaced persons, people who were afflicted in various ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to have displayed certain exhibits. Could the document bearing ERN 0468-7742 please be displayed. Mr. Grujic, are you able to see on the computer, is there ...

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to page 2 -- well, first let's scroll down a little bit on page 1. I see we're at the top of the page; let's scroll down slowly. And let's turn to page 2 of the B/C/S version of the document, which is pages 2 to 3 in the English version. Incidentally, I have also made hard copies of the English translation of this document. Could I have the assistance of the usher? Mr. Grujic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That is a statement that I wrote, and that describes -- it gives, first of all, my personal details, and then it describes the chronology of the establishment of this commission, later administration, the reasons why such an institution was created in the Republic of Croatia, going on to describe the purview of this commission and its activities that are listed one by one. It also describes the technical advisory body that is involved in this work, and the methodology of search for missing persons, mentioning as well the decrees that served as a basis for establishing these institutions, beginning with commissions and administrations, and each of these decrees also stipulates the field of expertise of these commissions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Did you provide this document during proofing last month?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: That's correct. That is a document that I produced last month.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And is it different from the statement that you had prepared earlier?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: To some extent, some details differ. When I gave my earlier statement, the organisational structure was different. What we had in existence was the Office for Prisoners and Missing Persons, which ceased to be in 2004 when the administration was established for prisoners and missing persons. So this statement was adapted to reflect the changes in the state structure and our organisation of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to page 11 in the B/C/S version. And in the English version, page 17 of the English version. Mr. Grujic, are there aspects here that are different from the earlier report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is clear that as time went by some missing persons were found and taken off the list of missing persons, and the number of found and identified persons was deducted from the list of missing persons and added to the number of persons killed. So from that day to date a number of new exhumations were performed, and a number of exhumed victims has increased, and also the number of identified victims has increased. So the only difference is in numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So would you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just get something clear? Persons that were found were deducted from the number of missing persons and added to the number of killed people. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You find a person, and then you add them to the number of killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A missing person can be found in two ways; it can be found alive, and in that case, we take measures to have that person released if he or she is in prison and to reunite them with their family. If the person is found dead, they can be in an individual grave or a mass grave. That is the second option. So when one of the missing persons is found in a mass grave, they are taken off the list of missing persons because they have been found. But since they are dead, we place them on the list of casualties, people killed. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have found the missing person's corpse, not the missing person, in that situation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, correct. That's if we find the body of the missing person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We must make that clear, make that distinction very clearly, because if you say you found a missing person, and then you are adding to the number of the dead ... A person is alive, but if you found a corpse, it's something different. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: So, Mr. Grujic, would you characterise this document, then, as your updated report?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Correct. But I have to say here in 31A you will read that the total number of identified remains is -- yes, this is the updated number at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence and assigned an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 291, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like the document bearing ERN 0469-0799 to be displayed, please. Could we turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This is a decree adopted by the government of the Republic of Croatia on the basis of which the Administration for Missing Persons was established, and it also describes the purview of the administration. Precisely in this Article 64, it says that the Administration for Imprisoned and Missing Persons deals with technical affairs related to the search for imprisoned and missing persons as well as exhumation and identification of remains from mass and individual graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 292, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like the document bearing ERN 0469-0796 to be displayed. And could we turn to the next page. Could we scroll down slowly. And let's turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are now on page 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Yes, we are. Let's scroll down as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are we looking for, Ms. Valabhji?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I was just trying to familiarise the witness with the document. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Witness, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This is the decree of the government of Croatia on establishing the Commission for Imprisoned and Missing Persons of the Republic of Croatia. I told you that in addition to the administration there was also a commission, precisely this commission, at whose document we are now looking. So this is the decree establishing this commission, or an office for detainees and missing persons as an interdepartmental body which included practically all relevant ministries in the Republic of Croatia dealing with detained and missing persons so the problem could be addressed as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 293, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could the document bearing ERN 0469-3240 now be shown. And let's turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This document is a questionnaire which is filled for every missing person. And this questionnaire is mentioned in the first document that came with my statement. You have the explanation of how this document was drafted. This is a document where all information on a missing person is entered. It has several sections. It lists personal, basic particulars of each missing person, also its status, the manner in which the person went missing, the place, persons who might be responsible for the fact that this person disappeared, also health information on the missing person needed in identification, as well as information about the person who is seeking the missing person. This questionnaire was created in such a way that specialists in criminal science, psychologists, and different other experts were included in creating it, so everybody who could provide a meaningful input into this process. This questionnaire was created in 1994 and it contains various elements recommended by the UN agencies, by ICRC, and so on, listing all the information needed, generally, to find a missing person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Incidentally, I have hard copies of the English translation - I should have distributed that earlier - of this questionnaire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: On e-court there is only the B/C/S version so far.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think that's right, and I hope the hard copies will assist in remedying that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document and its accompanying translation be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document and its accompanying translation be admitted into evidence and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 294, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: I would like a little bit more time to peruse the questionnaire. Not too long, just a little bit more time. Thank you. Thank you very much. I have completed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the document bearing ERN 0469-6078 please be exhibited [sic]. And let's turn to the next page, which is also the second page of the English version. It seems a little hard to read. I wonder if it can be made slightly bigger. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This is an organigramme of the structure of bodies participating in the process of exhumation and identification. It also describes the process. It lists the participants and describes their jobs in that process. Based on this scheme, you can see that the Ministry of Family -- the Ministry of Family and Intergenerational Solidarity Affairs prepares information on the missing persons in the places where mass graves are found, organises and coordinates exhumation, conducts preliminary identification, and then identification keeps records on exhumation and identification and collects full documentation on the process. On the right part of this organigramme we can see that international organisations participate in a transparent manner in this entire process and their experts are given opportunity to monitor the process. In everything that has been done from 1996 until today, we exhumed 140 mass graves and over 2.000 individual graves, and practically in all of these instances international observers took part. Then you can see the portion pertaining to the administration, and you can see which bodies participate in exhumation and their tasks. You will see that the Ministry of the Interior is listed here as a body which takes -- ensures that there is security; that it secures the place, it de-mines the area, and conducts certain technical steps on site, as well as keeps a record of exhumation. The following body which participates is Ministry of Defence, which is involved for purely logistical reasons. There is a department within the Ministry of Defence which deals almost exclusively with exhumations. They conduct engineering work on sites where mass graves and individual graves are located. They also transport remains and process them further. Then we have the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs. They ensure that doctors, specialists in forensic medicine are present, or pathologists, and they submit information to the Administration for Detained and Missing Persons, and coordinate that part of record-keeping. Then we have the Ministry of Justice, which ensures that an investigative judge is present who conducts the investigation, and then all relevant documents are submitted to the Administration for Detained and Missing Persons. In addition to these bodies, Croatian Red Cross is also involved as a humanitarian agency, which collects information needed for identification, it also contacts family members and invites them to be present. So they are actually a body who contacts the family to ensure that the family is present when exhumation and identification are conducted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, in your updated report you discuss various statistics concerning missing, exhumed, displaces and detained persons. I would like to discuss some of these statistics in greater detail, particularly in connection with various charts and tables.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And to that end, could the document bearing ERN 0469-3103 please be displayed. I see that it's the English version which is on the screen, and the English and B/C/S are, of course, part of the same document. Actually, I have a hard copy of the B/C/S version. Perhaps to facilitate matters, this could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have a hard copy for your opposite number?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't. The document that's currently displayed on the screen has the English followed by the B/C/S, so it's of course not going to be possible to show both versions simultaneously because they are in one and the same document, and I see -- Mr. Whiting has informed me that the witness already has a copy, in which case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I have my own copy. Both in Croatian and in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. So you would like to perhaps hand over the copy to your opposite number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to inform you that the Defence has a copy of this document, so everything is fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we turn to page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, please take a look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a chart showing exhumed persons. There are 3.568 so far, out of which 2.982 have been identified, or perhaps 84 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Who prepared this chart?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This document, and actually all charts, have been prepared in my office, and I took part in their creation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And when was it prepared?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: These are the most current data. This document was created last month.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, in what country did these exhumations take place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The exhumations depicted here took place in the territory of the Republic of Croatia in the areas which used to be temporarily occupied previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And during what period of time did these exhumations take place?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The said exhumations, the process of exhuming bodies was commenced in 1996 after the occupied territories had been liberated and after it was enabled -- after we were enabled access to this territory of Croatia, the newly reintegrated territory of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 5 of the document. Of course it's page 5 in both versions. Now, on this page the status -- pardon me -- yes, this chart lists several categories of persons, such as civilians and soldiers. How were these figures tabulated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: It is obvious that all members of armed forces of the Republic of Croatia were recorded by the Ministry of Veterans' Affairs and Intergenerational Solidarity. All of those whose names were recorded, based on the questionnaires that we mentioned earlier, were the sources based on which this data was compiled. The chart on the right side describes only those whose status was known. In the cases where the status was not known, we were unable to give analysis of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 296, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. May the document bearing ERN 0469-3089 please be shown. Perhaps if the usher -- I have the B/C/S, because I see the witness is looking for the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. Could we turn to page 2 of the document. Now, on this page the total number of killed persons is listed as 12.078. Witness, on what basis was this figure reached?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The list of persons who were killed was created on the basis of the decision of the government of Croatia by my office. The sources for compiling this single list were the list of persons who were killed, by the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia. These lists were unified and the number of exhumed persons was added to the list. At this point in time we can say with certainty that in the Republic of Croatia, at least - I'm repeating, at least - 12.078 persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, there's something I would like to understand that may very well be a problem of interpretation. There is a sentence here that says: "The sources for compiling this single list were the list of persons who were killed, by the Ministry of Health and Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia." Is that what is intended to be said?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Witness, could you -- did you understand His Honour's question pertaining to the response you just gave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My understanding of that statement is that these people were killed by the Ministry of Health and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, this must be an interpretation problem. As I have said, on the basis of lists compiled by these institutions in the course of their work -- I'm now describing events which took place 10 years ago. We took these lists, we unified them in my office where we keep official records on these persons, so the lists coming from these ministries were simply a source for creating this final list. We have details on each name entered on the list. The institutions which, at the time, were active in this field, namely the Ministry of Health, which received from the ground information on persons who were killed, they recorded this information, we took this information over from them, and created a single database on persons who were killed. I just wanted to explain how we came into possession of these details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to page 4 of this document. Mr. Grujic, what does this chart show in terms of the number of killed civilians? What is the figure that is shown?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Based on this chart, we can see that 4.508 persons were civilians, 782 persons, and their status is not known. We don't have reliable information about their status. But out of the total number, 6.788 were members of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, as to the figure relating to civilians, how was this statistic derived or tabulated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Just like information on all casualties, when information is recorded, the status of a person is also recorded. However, the situation is even clearer in this case: We have firm, reliable information. Even though 782 persons could be said that they were not members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, but we don't have firm information confirming that they were civilians. How is this possible? Members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia were recorded, their names were recorded. Their families today continue to receive certain benefits based on their status. In order to receive benefits, they need to submit a number of documents confirming that members of their family were members of armed forces. So we have a very firm, reliable figure in this case. It is clear that they are interested in receiving financial benefits. So let me repeat: In addition to being recorded by the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, in the case of these 6.788 persons, their family members receive, nowadays, financial benefits on the basis of the fact that their family members were members of armed forces of the Republic of Croatia and took part in combat. So we have a double source in this case to confirm their status, namely that of the members of armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this set of documents be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This set of documents is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number, and I apologise for not using the microphone earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask a question? By the set of documents, you mean this 14-page document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No, this is one question, I have a second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Yes, I meant the document that starts with ERN 0469-3089.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, and what I wanted to ask, how does this document relate to the former one about -- the chart about exhumed and identified persons? We had the number of 3.568 exhumed and identified persons, and then the last chart about 12.078 killed persons. How does this relate to each other? Is the exhumed -- are the exhumed persons part of the killed persons, and how did you do that? Just to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. 11.296 -- or rather, we have to say 12.078 is the total number firmly recorded as the number of deaths. That number, 12.078, includes victims exhumed from mass and individual graves, around 2.500 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So what is the 2.500? It says "around 2.500."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what is unclear. Where is that number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On the evidence, on the transcript, the witness said: "... as the number of -- That number, 12.078, includes victims exhumed from mass and individual graves, around 2.500." My question is, what does, "around 2.500" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It must be an error. It's not 2.500, it's -- the total number of exhumed, I will tell you the exact number, it's 3.568. Not 2.000, but 3.500.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is simply what does, "around 2.500" at the end of your answer at page 20, lines 2 to 4, to 5 mean? That's all. Is it something that came by mistake that shouldn't be there, or what -- does it have any significance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's obviously an error relating to the number of exhumed victims. What I said is that the total number of dead is 12.078, including the number of exhumed from mass and individual graves, which is not 2.500, but 3.568.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. Could we show the document bearing ERN -- has the previous document been assigned an exhibit number? I'm referring to 0469-3089.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what you collectively called a set.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And caused some confusion in the process. Okay. Thank you. Could we now show 0469-3071, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, have you located the document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 2. Mr. Grujic, what -- what are these charts about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This particular chart relates to missing persons and it's evident from it that at this time in the Republic of Croatia, we have 1.140 persons still missing. And this chart depicts the structure according to gender. We see that 970 men and 223 women are still recorded as missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And let's turn to page 7. What does this page illustrate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This page shows the number of missing persons by districts, by administrative units in the Republic of Croatia. It shows clearly that the greatest number of missing persons is in the Vukovar-Srijem county, 504; in Sisak-Moslavina county, 264 persons; Osijek-Baranja county, 88; and so on. It shows the number of missing persons according to the region where they went missing -- from which they went missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe this may just be an opportune time to ask my question which I was going to ask about all the other documents that have been handed in. I was going to ask, in fact, whether we have the data per region like that of the dead people, the 12.078, and all those other people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What kind of data? Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The data per region. You said, for instance, there were 12.078 people dead. In that document are we going to find a distribution of the 12.078 according to regions and districts, like you have done in this particular case? That was a question I was going to ask about the dead people and all the other statistics that you have given us so far, whether the statistics have been broken down in terms of districts like that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are not broken down by counties, but I have the ethnic structure that I can give you, the age structure and the gender breakdown of these numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that information in the analysis, in the data that you have filed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so. We have these numbers in these tables organised precisely in the way I just described. As Madam Prosecutor said, they are to be found in a set of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Coming back to this document that's on the screen, the 1.140 missing people, do we have names attached to all the 1.140? In other words, do we know who these people are who are missing? Otherwise, how do we get to that number of missing people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. We spoke earlier of a document that we named Questionnaire for Missing Persons. Each missing person has attached to them a questionnaire giving all their personal details, the circumstances, time and place of disappearance. Every missing person has a file, a name and surname, and behind each one of them there is a person looking for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That satisfies me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I just had one more question about this document. Turning to the next page, which is page 8 -- Turning to the next page, which is page 8, Mr. Grujic, can you tell us, during what period of time did these persons go missing?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Again, we're talking about the current situation, that is the total of 1.140 missing persons, each of whom, as I said, has a file, a dossier. On the basis of data from these dossier, we compiled these statistics which shows that out of this total number in 1991, 943 went missing, 113 went missing in 1992, 15 in 1993, 3 went missing in 1994, and 22 went missing in 1995. For 44 of them the year of disappearance is not known. I wanted to add one more thing. This is the current number of missing persons. But in 1991 the number of missing persons was 18.000. And their cases were resolved in various ways. As I said, missing persons can be found alive and reunited with their families, or released from prisons, or they can be found dead through exhumations. But currently we have this number, 1.140, as shown here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I see we've reached -- well, we are a little past the hour, Your Honour. Perhaps this would be a convenient time. Or we could also -- I was just going to ask that this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 298, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And indeed it does look like it is a convenient time to take the break. We will come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. Continuing with the documents, could the document bearing ERN 0469-3055 please be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, have you located the document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 2 of the document. What does this document pertain to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This document deals with people expelled from somewhere in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, and we see that there is a total of 220.338 expelled persons, out of which 105.036 are men, and 115.302 are women. Or, in terms of percentage, 52 per cent are women, and 47.7 per cent are men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And how was this figure of 220.338 reached?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: In the Republic of Croatia there is an office for expelled persons, or displaced persons that has registered each such person, and each of them has a dossier. So behind each of these numbers we have a name, surname, and personal details, and they are compatible, these numbers and data, with the data of the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And let's turn to the next page. What does this page illustrate, in a sentence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This shows the ethnic structure of displaced persons, those 220.338 persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 299, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's take a look at the document bearing ERN 0469-3033.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: What is this document about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: In this set of documents we have an analysis of imprisoned persons. 7.666 were recorded as held in camps and prisons of previously occupied areas in the Republic of Croatia, in Serbia, or in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And how was this figure derived?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: As I said in the introduction of my statement, the Administration for Imprisoned and Missing Persons keeps records on prisoners of war, and behind each number again there is a name and surname, the circumstances of detention or arrest, and release. Most of these people were also recorded by the International Red Cross as prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And what time period does this figure pertain to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The greatest number of detainees were released by 1992, and the last prisoner was released in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And, finally, let's turn to page 5 of the document. What does this page show?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: On this page we see the ethnic structure of imprisoned persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 300, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could I just ask two questions relating to this document. Is there a breakdown in terms of soldiers and civilians, of these numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In that document we see an indication of the status of the detainee. Where it says that 2.094 persons were recorded in the category of members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, whereas 1.865 were registered as civilians, and with regard to 3.614, the status is not determined. But we can go back again to what I said earlier, that family members of the members of the armed forces receive benefits, and therefore we can deduce that those 3.614 are not members of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You indicated a little earlier, Mr. Grujic, that the last detained person came out around 1995. Did I correctly hear you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 1996. Since 1996, after the last detainee had been released, has it not been possible to determine the nationality of the 24.5 per cent whose nationality is still undetermined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say that in the Republic of Croatia we have a law on confidentiality of information, so that data on ethnicity is not accessible without the express consent of each person concerned. So anybody who wished to declare their ethnicity has done so on previous occasions when information was gathered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Ms. Valabhji.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could the next document, bearing ERN number 0469-3252 please be displayed. Could it be enlarged a little bit? Please scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, can you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This document depicts the situation in the Bacin area; the number of residents and their structure in 1991, the number of displaced in that place. It says that in 1991 there were 414 residents, out of which 393 Croats, 9 unknown, and 6 Serbs, and 6 others. Out of that total number, 286 were registered as displaced or expelled. And, furthermore, 13 are still on record as missing. This statistical document says that 58 persons were exhumed in Bacin from one mass grave and two individual graves. Out of these 58, 44 bodies have been positively identified, and each them is categorised according to their ethnicity, gender and age.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Were you present at that exhumation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I took part in that process, beginning with the search for the location, through the organisation and implementation of this exhumation, up to the identification of bodies found.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page of this document. What is -- what does this page show, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: On this page we see information about Hrvatska Dubica, which is adjacent to Bacin, and we see that in 1991 the population of Hrvatska Dubica was 2.062. 694 were expelled, 12 are still recorded as missing, 7 persons -- 7 bodies were exhumed, out of which 6 were positively identified, and they were exhumed from individual graves. And again we see breakdowns by ethnicity, age and gender.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page. Could you tell us what this page illustrates.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Once again we see that the structure is the same. It is described here that in a place called Cerovljani in 1991, there were 512 residents, and we see their ethnic make-up. 203 persons were recorded as deported or expelled. We see their age breakdowns, we also see that two persons are still listed as missing, two persons from Cerovljani. Further on we see that three bodies were exhumed in Cerovljani, out of which all three were positively identified, and then we see their gender, ethnic and age breakdown. And then we see that their bodies were exhumed from individual graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we on the same page? We've got Skabrnja on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have Cerovljani.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, when -- probably the pages have been somehow changed around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's put it down to our inability to deal with technology.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed it was technology.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I won't be going through all the pages of this document. At this time I would simply ask that it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 301, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You don't want it admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I would very much like it to be admitted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, prior to coming here to testify, were you asked to review certain lists of victims contained in the indictment in this case and to check them against the records kept by your office on killed, exhumed and missing persons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I analysed the list of victims from the indictment and I compared it with the list and official records kept by my office. And in relation to each of these places, or rather, in relation to each of them, we made an analysis covering each name. That is to say, covering each name and each place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could the document bearing ERN 0469-3261 please be displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While that document is being displayed, Mr. Grujic, can I just ask, did you have a similar analysis relating to detained people? The question had been to you whether you had anything to -- any analysis relating to killed, exhumed and missing persons. I know there are no longer detained persons, but did you have a similar thing with respect to those who were detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not in this manner as I did here. I did an analysis here because there are names given in the indictment. But certainly the analysis of detained persons could also be done. We know which prisons existed, camps, and who was detained where. We have that information. But we did not do that type of analysis at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could we see the document bearing ERN 0469-3261. And I have some hard copies of this document. Could I have the assistance of the usher? This is actually the translation of the document, and I don't think it's in e-court, so that necessitates the distribution of hard copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document that I mentioned, the document representing the analysis of the victims mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to page 2 of the document. Can you explain to us how this list was annotated? What does it show, and how was it annotated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the left side you have family name and then first name and then the date of birth. This pertains to victims listed in the indictment. Following that, on the right-hand side, after the date of birth, we have the column indicating the gender of victims, and then the next category is -- the next column reflects what happened to the victim. And it can be interpreted using the key that is enclosed with this document. In relation to the first name, Katarina Alavancic, we see that she was born on the 10th of November, 1910, she's of female gender, and the category indicates that she has been identified. Then we have the next column, entitled, "Circumstances." She was found in a mass grave, in a place called Skela, exhumed on the 13th -- on the 25th of March, 1997. She was identified -- or she was recorded previously as an unidentified victim under the number given here, and then she was identified on the 18th of March, 1999. And then we have similar explanations given for all other victims. In instances where we have abbreviation "ND," that means that we have no information pertaining to the person listed in the indictment. If the abbreviation "NES" is seen, that means that that person is still listed as missing. Abbreviation "CPO" stands for the fact that a request was submitted to locate mortal remains. So such a procedure can be initiated in cases where a person is listed as missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: This list that we're currently looking at, which location does it pertain to? Let's scroll up, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This pertains to Bacin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to page 4 of this document. It's ERN 3264. There are three lines in bold. Could you explain those three lines?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: In these cases these persons were found alive. They were previously listed as missing, and they were found alive, so the seeking procedure was terminated in their cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next page. What location does this pertain to, this list?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The analysis was made in the same way as in the case of Bacin. This pertains to Lipovaca Dreznicka, that's the name of the place, and we have seven persons in this location.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next page. Again, where does this pertain to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This analysis pertains to Vukovici. We have 10 persons on the list, out of which two have been identified, four were established to be dead, one is missing, and we have no information concerning three persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Going to the next page, what area or place does this list refer to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This list represents an analysis conducted in the same way, and it pertains to Saborsko. In Saborsko we have 28 persons on this list, out of which 27 were identified, and one person is recorded as killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next page. What location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we go to the next page, can we just take a moment on Saborsko. The one person is recorded as killed, the rest -- or we've got to go back to the -- are the rest alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. All 28 persons were killed. Out of those 28, however, one person, before the exhumation, was recorded as killed in the list including 12.000 people, whereas in case of these 27 persons, their bodies were found in two mass graves in Saborsko, and also in some individual graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And turning to the next page, which location does this list pertain to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This list pertains to Skabrnja. The list has names of 38 persons. All of them are also recorded in the list of persons killed containing 12.000 and something names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: The next page, please?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The next page deals with Nadin. There are seven persons on the list. All seven are also listed as identified, meaning they were exhumed and identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just go through one more page. The next page, please. What does this page show?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This page takes us back to Skabrnja, however in this case it deals with a different event. This list has 26 persons, all 26 were identified, and all of them, all 26, were buried -- or rather, I apologise, 25 were buried in the mass grave in Skabrnja, which was exhumed between the 5th and 6th of June, 1996. All persons on this list were identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. And may it please be -- the document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 302, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Can I ask something about the last page we were just looking at? Referring to the second event, as it says, and it says 18 November, 1991 to February 1992, whereas the first page concerning Skabrnja refers to 18 and 19 November, 1991. So is this a distinct list but still also concerning 18th of November 1991, in part, or what can we say about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Witness, His Honour has asked a question regarding the last list and its temporal frame in comparison with the other list we saw on Skabrnja, which says 18th to 19th November, 1991. Is there an overlap? Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Well, I will try to explain. The first list, the first one we mentioned involving Skabrnja, clearly has to do with the victims who were killed on the 18th and 19th of November. These victims -- or their bodies, following some local negotiations, were turned over to their families. At the time, we knew nothing about the circumstances of their death and exhumation, we simply had a situation where we had mortal remains delivered in 1991. Let me verify the year to make sure that I didn't make a mistake. In 1992 these remains were handed over, and it was then that we recorded these persons as killed. Autopsies were conducted, and there are records of them. In case of the second event, we found a mass grave in Skabrnja. We exhumed it on the 5th and 6th of June, 1996. And there we have all records concerning the entire process of exhumation and identification. So, yes, there is some temporal overlap, because some of these people, based on eye-witness testimony, were killed in 1991, between November of 1991 and February of 1992. I don't have more specific information about the exact time of death. I just have information about the place and time of exhumation. And in relation to that, we have all relevant data, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Could the document bearing ERN 0469-3121 please be shown. Could we enlarge it somewhat?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what is this document? Who prepared it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This document was prepared by the Crisis Staff of the Ministry of Health, information and investigation department. These documents were forwarded to my office, because my office kept records on casualties. This document pertains to the civilians who were killed in the course of the artillery attack on Zagreb on the 2nd and 3rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 of the document - it's page 2 in both the English and B/C/S versions - what is written under the headings "Weapons," and "Targets"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Under the heading "Weapons," we see that there were 12 missiles, six -- and six each in attack. They were of a type called Orkan, and they had cluster filling. This type of a weapon is intended to produce as large a number of personnel casualties as possible without significant property damage. These weapons are banned by international conventions. And then under "Targets," we see that the targets were all in the centre of the town and its vicinity, and then we see what particular houses were hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 303, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

In a total of four locations exhumation was conducted, and we have a record of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Incidentally, where is Rakovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: It is located in the Karlovac district. And I'll give you more precise data now. The exhumations that were performed were performed in the places I already enumerated, Lipovacka Dreznica, a site which is not far from Slunj town.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And did you participate in these exhumations?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there all the time, but I visited and supervised the process, and I think you can see that from the record. According to our prevailing rules, I supervised the drafting of the records and I toured regularly during exhumations, but I wasn't there throughout the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number 304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take a look now at 65 ter number 402. Let's scroll down slowly. And let's look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Is the document part of the records kept by your office?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a dossier of a missing person that has been kept by my office all the time. And this particular person was taken off the list of missing persons and added to the list of deaths, because her remains were found in a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Turning to page 6 of the B/C/S version, which is also page 6 in the English version, could you read aloud the information under item 5 of the section entitled, "Information on abduction, disappearance and capture." utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: The dossier of a missing person contains a chapter that reflects the circumstances of disappearance or arrest of that person. The last question is: Were there other persons who were forcibly taken away, together with the missing person? The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI

utterances.text: Microphone please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you can look at the last page that we looked at -- I don't know whether it was page 8. Let's see. No. That's at page 2. At the bottom of that page I see there's a section 2 there, "Victims," and there is no number. Is there any significance of the lack of a number? At the bottom of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think the document continues. Probably the rest of that is appearing on the following page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It does look like that's there. Thank you so much, it's just that we didn't go to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: As the final aspect of the direct examination, I would now like to play a few clips from a video. The first clip is slightly on the long side. I think it's approximately 12 minutes or so. I wonder if the actual clip, is it only -- can it only be shown in that size?

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I neglected to mention what the video is about, Your Honours. This is a video concerning certain exhumations. And after we play the first clip, I'll be asking the witness some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Valabhji. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, do you recognise this video clip?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a documentary which covered the location of Bacin. The film depicts the process of exhumation and identification of the bodies of victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Is it accurate? Is the clip accurate?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everything we saw is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review the entire video itself during proofing last month?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I'd like to now show the remaining clips. Now, they are considerably shorter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: And the final clip, which is much, much shorter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, what was the name of the place shown in the final -- in the third and final clip?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: It was -- the distance from the designated place is 10 kilometres [as interpreted] relative to the mass grave, from the site where a mass grave was found. And it's just by the edge of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this video be admitted into evidence? I have copies of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The clip is admitted into evidence. May it be given an exhibit number. But did you get the answer to the question, what is the name of the place? Mr. Grujic talked about the distance from the designated place being 10 kilometres. I'm not quite sure what the designated place is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: I think he may have mentioned it at the outset when we watched the first clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: But, Mr. Grujic, could you tell us the name of this region? First of all, where the mass grave is, was found.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC
utterances.text: This footage, especially the last frame, was made at the entrance to Bacin village, and the place that was marked by police tape, where there was a concentration of cartridges, was just 10 metres away from the mass grave, along the edge of the road. So the place is Bacin, the site of the mass grave, and 10 metres from the mass grave there were cartridges found.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
utterances.text: Thank you. That's now very clear. I think the previous translation said 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VALABHJI
